segments.t: In the recording studio, Julien Dore learns that television executives have refused to finance his movie. Furious over an absurd misunderstanding, Julien threatens to quit the project while Gabriel and Sofia urge him to persist. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
France 2 refuse de financer notre film!
Qu'est-ce qui se passe exactement ce matin?
C'est un refus total, pas d'argent!
Alors notre grand projet est complètement mort?
Il doit y avoir un simple malentendu.
Élisabeth prétend qu'il y a un scandale.
Mais de quel scandale parles-tu donc?
Elle a inventé un mot totalement absurde.
Je vais vérifier cette histoire bizarre maintenant.
Ce mot n'existe nulle part, regarde!
Ils détruisent trois ans de mon travail!
Nous pouvons trouver un autre financement ailleurs.
Non, c'est fini, je laisse tomber.
Julien, garde espoir pour ce beau film.
Ne baisse pas les bras si vite, Julien.
Let's examine how Julien reacts to the funding cancellation and how Gabriel tries to rescue the film step by step.
France 2 refuse de financer notre film!
'France 2 refuses to finance our film!' Whenever 'refuse' precedes an action in French, 'of' bridges the two — literally 'refuses of financing'.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe exactement ce matin?
'What is happening exactly this morning?' Opening with 'what is it that passes itself', Gabriel tacks 'exactly' and 'this morning' onto the end in French.
C'est un refus total, pas d'argent!
'It is a total refusal, no money!' Even in a two-word fragment like 'no money!', French uses 'not of money' in the negative.
Alors notre grand projet est complètement mort?
'So our big project is completely dead?' Calling a plan or deal 'dead' is a super common everyday expression in French when an idea falls flat.
Il doit y avoir un simple malentendu.
'There must be a simple misunderstanding.' Look at the closing word: 'misunderstanding' in French is built from 'badly' plus 'heard' — literally something misheard!
Élisabeth prétend qu'il y a un scandale.
'Elisabeth claims that there is a scandal.' Major false-friend alert: what looks like English 'pretends' means 'claims' or 'alleges' in French!
Mais de quel scandale parles-tu donc?
'But what scandal are you talking about?' Tucked onto the end of a question in French, the word that usually means 'therefore' adds puzzled emphasis — closer to 'what on earth?'.
Elle a inventé un mot totalement absurde.
'She invented a totally absurd word.' Here 'word' is the crisp three-letter cousin of English 'motto', followed by two transparent cognates meaning 'totally absurd'.
Je vais vérifier cette histoire bizarre maintenant.
'I will verify this strange story now.' Where 'verify' sounds formal in English, its French cognate is what you'd say casually for looking something up on your phone.
Ce mot n'existe nulle part, regarde!
'This word exists nowhere, look!' In the negative, French expresses 'nowhere' as 'not ... in null part' — literally 'in no part'.
Ils détruisent trois ans de mon travail!
'They destroy three years of my work!' French uses the plain present here where English says 'they are ruining', built on the same root as 'destruction'.
Nous pouvons trouver un autre financement ailleurs.
'We can find another financing elsewhere.' Unlike English single-word 'another', French keeps 'an' and 'other' separate, closing on a cousin of 'alibi' meaning 'elsewhere'.
Non, c'est fini, je laisse tomber.
'No, it is finished, I give up.' Literally 'I let fall', that closing idiom is how you'll hear French speakers say 'I give up' or 'forget about it'.
Julien, garde espoir pour ce beau film.
'Julien, keep hope for this beautiful film.' Dropping the 's' off 'you keep' creates the warm casual 'you' command 'keep hope'.
Ne baisse pas les bras si vite, Julien.

'Do not give up so quickly, Julien.' Literally 'do not lower the arms' — like a boxer dropping his guard — this vivid French idiom means 'don't throw in the towel'. Now let's listen to the whole dialogue again.
France 2 refuse de financer notre film!
Qu'est-ce qui se passe exactement ce matin?
C'est un refus total, pas d'argent!
Alors notre grand projet est complètement mort?
Il doit y avoir un simple malentendu.
Élisabeth prétend qu'il y a un scandale.
Mais de quel scandale parles-tu donc?
Elle a inventé un mot totalement absurde.
Je vais vérifier cette histoire bizarre maintenant.
Ce mot n'existe nulle part, regarde!
Ils détruisent trois ans de mon travail!
Nous pouvons trouver un autre financement ailleurs.
Non, c'est fini, je laisse tomber.
Julien, garde espoir pour ce beau film.
Ne baisse pas les bras si vite, Julien.
Despite the sudden setback from France 2, Gabriel and Sofia stand firmly by Julien's artistic vision. Let's review the financing and crisis-management vocabulary from this scene. See you next time!
À demain!
